function.name: player_stats_getLastGame
function.description: Get last game statistics for a specific player in basketball Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

player_name.description: The name of the basketball player.

team.description: The team that player currently plays for.

metrics.description: Specific metrics to retrieve. If no value is specified, all available metrics will be returned by default.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to get stats from previous game for LeBron James (points and rebounds). We need to call the function with appropriate arguments.

We have function `player_stats_getLastGame` expecting:

- player_name: string
- team: string
- metrics? optional array or single metric?

It says metrics can be "Points", "Rebounds", "Assists", "Blocks". It might accept an array but not sure; we should pass ["Points","Rebounds"] maybe as list. But spec shows type union: `"Points" | "Rebounds" | "Assists" | "Blocks"` which suggests it's one element only. However typical usage may allow multiple values. We'll just provide both separately? Might cause error if expects single string. Let's check specification: In description it says "Specific metrics to retrieve. If no value is specified, all available metrics will be returned by default." So likely accepts array. Provide array.

Thus call function with:

{
    player_name:"LeBron James",
    team:"Los Angeles Lakers",
    metrics:["Points","Rebounds"]
}

But note team could also be "Lakers"? Use full official name: Los Angeles Lakers.

Let's produce JSON accordingly.
